docs.name: My Engagement Score
docs.where: A card on your Home dashboard.
docs.purpose: A score out of 100 that shows how actively you take part in learning, with a trend so you can see if it is going up or down.
steps: Open Home and find the My Engagement Score card.
Press the small refresh button on the card to update it.
notes: It is built from five kinds of activity: Video watching, Quiz participation, Assignment submission, Live class attendance, and Doubts and interactions.
The bands are: Highly Engaged 80 to 100, Moderately Engaged 60 to 79, Low Engagement 40 to 59, Very Low Engagement 0 to 39.
To raise it, do more of those five things, for example watch the class videos, join live classes, and hand in assignments on time.

docs.name: Flashcards
docs.where: Second tab on the Daily Review page, next to Daily Review.
docs.purpose: Quick exam-style flip cards made from your own textbook, so they match what you learn in class.
steps: Open the Flashcards tab and pick a subject, then a chapter.
Wait a moment while the cards are made. It can take up to half a minute.
Flip each card, then rate it Easy, Medium or Difficult. On a keyboard the keys 1, 2 and 3 do the same.
notes: Cards you rate Difficult come back sooner so you can master them.
If a card looks wrong you can report it, and you can stop seeing a card you do not want.

docs.name: Academic Tests
docs.purpose: Practice tests for your class and subject. You choose the setup, answer one question at a time, see straight away whether you were right, and finish with a score. Past tests are listed under Recent Tests.
steps: In Start a New Test, check your Class and pick a Subject.
Optionally type a Topic, and set the Number of Questions and the Level of Difficulty.
Press Generate & Start Test.
For each question choose an answer and press Confirm Answer, then Next Question. The last one says View Results.
notes: You see your score out of the total, the number correct and incorrect, your percentage, an encouraging message (Outstanding!, Great Job!, Good Effort! or Keep Practicing!) and a review of each question. The test also appears under Recent Tests. If you score below 50%, APAS sends a Performance Alert to your parent.
problems: The Subject list is empty. - Your school has no subjects set up for that class yet. Try a different class if you picked the wrong one, otherwise tell your teacher or school admin.
The Subject box is greyed out. - Choose a Class first. The subjects depend on it.
The Subject box says your profile has no school. - Your account is not linked to a school, so subjects cannot load. Ask your school admin to check your account.

docs.name: Adaptive Test
docs.purpose: A test that adjusts to you. The questions get easier or harder depending on your answers, so it can work out your level in fewer questions.
steps: Choose how wide the test is: Whole subject, This chapter, This topic, or Just this concept.
Pick the Subject, then the Chapter, Topic and optionally a Concept, and start.
Answer each question and press Next Question. Press See Results at the end.
notes: If you leave a test part-way it can resume where you stopped. Exit test asks you to confirm first.
The results show Accuracy, Questions, Your marks and a Skill breakdown.
A score can be marked provisional when many of the questions are still new. It becomes more precise over time.
If your school has negative marking on, wrong answers can lose marks, and the test shows you the rules.

docs.name: Daily Review
docs.where: Left menu, Daily Review (first tab of the Daily Review and Flashcards page).
docs.purpose: A short daily set of questions on things you learned earlier, timed so you practise each concept just before you would forget it. It keeps what you learn in your memory.
steps: Open Daily Review. The top shows how many are Due now, Later today, in the Next 7 days, and Locked in (21d+).
Choose an answer and press Submit, then Next. The last one says Finish.
When you are done, Check for more looks for any new reviews.
notes: You're all caught up means nothing is due right now. Come back when the next review is due.
Some concepts can be due but have no practice questions yet. The screen tells you when that is the case.

docs.name: Fees (profile tab)
docs.purpose: Shows the fee plan your school assigned when your admission was confirmed: the fee structure name, class, academic year and due date, a breakdown of each fee, the total fee, any concession or discount, how much is paid so far, and the outstanding balance. A badge shows whether it is Paid, Part paid, Pending or Overdue.
notes: It is view-only. You cannot change or pay from this tab.
Your parents pay from their own fee payment page. Questions about an amount are for the school's fee office.
If it says No admission fee plan linked, the plan appears once your admission is confirmed and the plan is linked to you.
docs.content:
Fees (profile tab)
Where: Student Profile, Fees tab.
What it is: Shows the fee plan your school assigned when your admission was confirmed: the fee structure name, class, academic year and due date, a breakdown of each fee, the total fee, any concession or discount, how much is paid so far, and the outstanding balance. A badge shows whether it is Paid, Part paid, Pending or Overdue.
Good to know: It is view-only. You cannot change or pay from this tab. Your parents pay from their own fee payment page. Questions about an amount are for the school's fee office. If it says No admission fee plan linked, the plan appears once your admission is confirmed and the plan is linked to you.
